reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch reject predestination to evil, reading Romans' vessels of wrath as God ratifying self-chosen wickedness rather than authoring it.

discrepancy.note: Ingersoll condemns the Calvinist reading of texts like Romans 9 as making God will the damnation of most of mankind for his own glory.

quotes.text: fellow-men are doomed to suffer eternal torment, to the end that their Creator may be eternally glorified.
quotes.attr: Robert G. Ingersoll (d. 1899), The Christian Religion, pt. III, Rejoinder to Judge Black (1881), on Romans 9:18 and 1 Timothy 2:4.
